newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ fin ministers reconfirm post-1998 tax cut aims.
newsitem.headline: NZ fin ministers reconfirm post-1998 tax cut aims.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch and Treasurer Winston Peters on Friday reconfirmed the government's tax cut plans after 1998.

They said in a joint statement that if the September referendum voted in favour of compulsory superannuation and fiscal and economic conditions permitted the government would introduce tax cuts in 1999, 2000, 2001 and 2002 equivalent to two percent in 1999 and one percent in each of the following three years.

"If the referendum does not support a compulsory superannuation scheme, and if economic and fiscal conditions permit, the government will consider further tax reductions in 1999-2000 and future years," the ministers said.
On Wednesday, Peters said in a speech that tax cuts would not be possible if the current state-funded superannuation scheme remained in place.

Opposition leader Helen Clark said Peters' Wednesday statement had contradicted statements made by Birch to the finance and expenditure committee that the post-1998 tax cuts would remain a priority for the government if the refernedum
"The government's goal is to reduce taxes at a rate that is consistent with meeting priority social needs and maintaining control of Crown debt," Birch and Peters said on Friday.

They said the top three priorities for the tax work programme for 1999-2000 would be implementing the tax policy initiatives in the December coalition agreement, protecting the tax base and publishing discusson documents.

The tax base work would include reviews of the use of passive investment funds by superannuation funds, GST on travel vouchers issued overseas and the taxation of restrictive covenants and lease inducement payments.
